name: Naked Raygun
label: Homestead
lede: Two Naked Raygun members moonlighted in Big Black, the band kept writing the Chicago punk songs other bands still cover, and in 2015 it opened for the Foo Fighters at Wrigley Field.

eras.title: A singer for a band that had none
eras.text: Two guitar-and-bass guys at a Chicago bar decide the city needs a punk band and go get Jeff Pezzati to sing in it. Within three years the band has a first EP, and two of its members have been borrowed by Steve Albini.

years.cap: The original lineup: Durango, Marko Pezzati, Jeff Pezzati
years.src: Chicago Punk Database · There's Something Hard in There
years.h: Two guys at O'Banion's, fed up, and a singer with a brother
years.p: [[Santiago Durango|00aa2c29-22a9-4e55-a01b-e51896a379a3]] and Marko Pezzati meet at the Chicago bar O'Banion's, decide the city lacks punk bands, and recruit Marko's brother Jeff to sing.
years.xp:
The Chicago Punk Database dates the meeting to February 1980. Jeff Pezzati has said he first came along to practices to give his vocal cords a workout, and stayed.

Durango wrote most of the early songs. Pezzati remembers him changing every song each time the band came to practice, then calling it by the same name.

years.src: Wikipedia: Basement Screams
years.h: The Morgan Street sessions capture the original lineup
years.p: Demos cut on Morgan Street in Chicago show the band before it changed. They sat unreleased until 1999.
years.xp: Eight of those 1982 tracks, including covers and alternate versions, became bonus material on the 1999 Quarterstick reissue of Basement Screams. The reissue notes describe an original lineup that would change significantly before the first full-length.

years.src: Wikipedia: Basement Screams · Chicago Punk Database
years.h: Basement Screams EP on Ruthless
years.p: Six songs, mostly by Durango, with saxophone on a few, on the same Chicago label that also had [[Big Black|9463868f-edc8-427e-ac07-ea89698e5f15]] and the [[Effigies|13e4a71f-7cc3-441e-901c-fab71c5c4338]].
years.xp:
Basement Screams was produced by Tim Powell. Steve Albini, who would soon be borrowing two of its members, wrote the liner notes for the 1999 reissue.

In the ChicagoPunk database's telling, Albini had praised the early Raygun guitar sound as something that would flatten everybody, and described it as underwater.

years.cap: Big Black around Bulldozer, with Pezzati and Durango
years.src: Wikipedia: Big Black · Wikipedia: Steve Albini
years.h: [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] borrows the singer and the guitarist
years.p: Albini meets Jeff Pezzati through friends, gets him to play bass in [[Big Black|9463868f-edc8-427e-ac07-ea89698e5f15]], and Santiago Durango wanders downstairs and joins too.
years.xp:
Big Black rehearsed in Pezzati's basement. Durango, Pezzati's bandmate in Naked Raygun, came down one day and asked to play. Both are on Big Black's Bulldozer EP, released in December 1983.

Albini was never in Naked Raygun. The traffic ran the other way: two of its members went into his band, and Pezzati left it in late 1984 over his job, an engagement and Raygun's schedule, replaced by Dave Riley. Albini later said of Durango that he ended up absolutely crucial to Big Black.

years.src: Wikipedia: Big Black · There's Something Hard in There · Wikipedia: Santiago Durango
years.h: Durango picks Big Black; John Haggerty takes his guitar
years.p: Durango leaves Naked Raygun to commit to Big Black. John Haggerty arrives on guitar.
years.xp: Haggerty's crisp, Buzzcocks-like tone, as Pezzati describes it, became the sound of the next stretch. Durango stayed with Big Black until it ended in 1987, then went to law school and formed Arsenal, which released two EPs on Touch and Go.

eras.title: Homestead, and a lineup that sticks
eras.text: Pezzati steps out of Big Black, a debut album from 1983 finally comes out on Homestead, and Pierre Kezdy and Eric Spicer lock in the rhythm section that carries the band for the rest of its first run.

years.src: Wikipedia: Throb Throb · Wikipedia: Homestead Records · There's Something Hard in There
years.h: Throb Throb: the debut LP, on Homestead
years.p: Recorded in 1983 but out in 1985 on Homestead, with a blueprint-style lyric sheet and a cover by Chicago comics artist Mike Saenz.
years.xp:
Homestead was a Long Island label started in 1983 as a sub-label of the importer Dutch East India Trading, and it also carried Sonic Youth, Big Black and Dinosaur Jr. This was the first album with Haggerty on guitar. Only Pezzati and bassist Camilo Gonzalez remained from the founding band.

Pezzati says a soundman at Chicago's Cobra Lounge told him that not a week goes by without a band covering Rat Patrol. The album was produced by Iain Burgess.

q: Pierre Kezdy's bass sounds like a power tool.
years.src: Wikipedia: Pierre Kezdy · There's Something Hard in There
years.h: Pierre Kezdy and Eric Spicer join, and Gonzalez goes
years.p: The bass-and-drums pair that will play on every album through 1990 arrives for the sessions that become All Rise.
years.xp: Kezdy was the younger brother of John Kezdy, singer of the Effigies. Chicago Tribune critic Greg Kot wrote that his bass sounds like a power tool.

years.src: Wikipedia: All Rise · There's Something Hard in There · Psychedelic Baby
years.h: All Rise: the first record by the four who stay
years.p: Jeff Pezzati wrote eight of its eleven songs; Albini did design work on the sleeve.
years.xp: Recorded in 1985 at Chicago Recording Company with Iain Burgess. Robert Christgau gave it a B. Pezzati has said the cover shows him dressed up and photographed in a railyard.

eras.title: Caroline, Europe and the Ramones
eras.text: Raygun leaves Homestead for Caroline, plays rooms in the thousands, and puts out the record that sells best. It is also the last one with Haggerty's guitar.

years.cap: Flyer or photo, Aragon Ballroom, Chicago, 1987
years.src: There's Something Hard in There
years.h: Sharing the Aragon Ballroom with the Ramones
years.p: Pezzati recalls playing the same bill as the [[Ramones|d6ed7887-a401-47a8-893c-34b967444d26]] at the Aragon in Chicago.
years.xp: Pezzati also recalls a night at the Riviera in Chicago that packed in 3,000 people.

years.src: Wikipedia: Jettison · Psychedelic Baby
years.h: Jettison: first of three on Caroline
years.p: Made at Jericho Studio and Chicago Recording Company with Iain Burgess and Larry Sturm of Ministry, then taken on long tours of Europe.
years.xp: Haggerty plays saxophone as well as guitar on the record. A live cover of Stiff Little Fingers' Suspect Device appears on the 1999 reissue.

years.big: Top seller, and its singer thinks it reached backward
q: I think the album suffers a little bit because of that.
years.src: Wikipedia: Understand? · There's Something Hard in There · Psychedelic Baby
years.h: Understand? is the biggest seller and Pezzati has notes
years.p: Recorded at Tanglewood in Brookfield, Illinois with Larry Sturm, artwork by Phil Hale, and a track, Hip Swingin', about U.S. meddling in South America.
years.xp:
Pezzati told There's Something Hard in There that the band was reaching for something it had written before and trying to recreate it. Hip Swingin' turned up in the 2018 movie Tag.

In Europe, Psychedelic Baby reports, the record was picked up country by country by different Virgin subsidiaries.

eras.title: Haggerty walks, Stephens steps in
eras.text: The guitarist who defined the sound leaves to start his own band, and Bill Stephens finishes out the run with one more album before Raygun stops.

years.src: Chicago Punk Database · Wikipedia: Pegboy · There's Something Hard in There
years.h: John Haggerty leaves to start Pegboy
years.p: He forms Pegboy with his brother Joe, Larry Damore and Steve Saylors; Bill Stephens takes over guitar.
years.xp: Sources put his exit in 1989 or 1990. The ChicagoPunk database points to friction over how often the band toured and who managed it. Pegboy's first EP, Three-Chord Monte, was the first release on Quarterstick Records.

years.src: Wikipedia: Raygun...Naked Raygun · Psychedelic Baby
years.h: Raygun...Naked Raygun: last album of the first run
years.p: Bill Stephens' first record, with Keith Auerbach co-producing, opens with Kezdy's Home.
years.xp: Kot called the record a pull-off that kept the band's hard edge. AllMusic's Bob Gendron said the missing Haggerty left it short on passion and tension. Pezzati says the label demanded changes to artwork and songs.

years.src: Wikipedia: Naked Raygun · Psychedelic Baby
years.h: Naked Raygun stops
years.p: The band goes quiet after 1992; one interview dates the end to 1991.

eras.title: Side projects and a two-show reunion
eras.text: Kezdy plays in Pegboy, the catalog gets reissued, and in 1997 the band plays two shows and records with Albini.

years.src: Wikipedia: Pegboy · Wikipedia: Pierre Kezdy
years.h: Kezdy joins Pegboy on bass
years.p: He follows Steve Albini, who had filled in on bass for Pegboy's Fore EP.

years.src: Wikipedia: Naked Raygun · Psychedelic Baby
years.h: Two reunion shows, and a session with Albini
years.p: The shows become the live album Free Shit in 2001; four songs cut with Albini at Electric appear on the Last of the Demohicans CD.
years.xp: Last of the Demohicans came out on Dyslexic Records in 1997. Free Shit followed on Haunted Town in 2001.

years.src: Wikipedia: Naked Raygun · Wikipedia: Basement Screams · Wikipedia: Throb Throb
years.h: Quarterstick reissues the back catalog
years.p: Bonus tracks go on the CDs, Albini writes the Basement Screams liner notes, and 400 copies of Throb Throb are pressed on green vinyl.

eras.title: Back for good, at a punk festival
eras.text: A reunion at Riot Fest becomes a permanent band, a documentary and a run of new singles.

years.src: Wikipedia: Riot Fest · Wikipedia: Naked Raygun · Wikipedia: Pierre Kezdy
years.h: Riot Fest brings them back, and they announce they are staying
years.p: The Raygun...Naked Raygun lineup of Jeff Pezzati, Bill Stephens, Eric Spicer and Pierre Kezdy plays Chicago's Riot Fest.
years.xp: Riot Fest was founded in Chicago in 2005 by Mike Petryshyn and Sean McKeough, and is known for reunions. Kezdy left Pegboy in 2007, and Mike Thompson later took over that band's bass.

years.src: Wikipedia: Naked Raygun
years.h: What Poor Gods We Do Make documentary DVD
years.p: A film on the band's story, with a CD of music, comes out on Riot Fest Records.

years.src: Wikipedia: Naked Raygun
years.h: First new studio songs since 1997: the Series 1 7-inch
years.p: Mein Iron Maiden and Out of Your Mind on red-and-cream vinyl; Series 2 and 3 follow in 2010 and 2011.

years.src: Wikipedia: Naked Raygun · Wikipedia: Pierre Kezdy
years.h: Kezdy has a stroke; Pete Mittler steps in
years.p: The Methadones' Pete Mittler joins so Kezdy can recover.

eras.title: Wrigley Field, a loss and a new record
eras.text: Fritz Doreza takes the bass, Foo Fighters hand them a baseball stadium, and Pierre Kezdy's last recordings end up on the first album in over 30 years.

years.src: Wikipedia: Naked Raygun · Wikipedia: Pierre Kezdy
years.h: Fritz Doreza joins; Kezdy returns on baritone guitar
years.p: Kezdy plays live again on baritone guitar; Doreza covers bass.

years.src: Wikipedia: Naked Raygun · Wikipedia: Jeff Pezzati
years.h: Opening for the Foo Fighters at Wrigley Field
years.p: The bill includes Urge Overkill and Cheap Trick; Dave Grohl has credited Raygun with sparking his interest in punk.
years.xp: A year earlier the band had opened for Bad Religion, the Offspring and Stiff Little Fingers on the Summer Nationals tour.

years.src: Wikipedia: Pierre Kezdy · Wikipedia: Over the Overlords
years.h: Pierre Kezdy dies of cancer, aged 58
years.p: The bassist had played with Raygun from the 1980s and finished his parts for the new record before he died.

years.src: Wikipedia: Over the Overlords · There's Something Hard in There · Psychedelic Baby
years.h: Over the Overlords: 31 years since the last one
years.p: Out on Wax Trax!, recorded over years with Steven Gillis, mastered by Ted Jensen.
years.xp:
The lead single's video was shot at Chicago's Cobra Lounge and includes fans' home performances. A track, Ode to Sean McKeough, honors the Cobra Lounge owner and Riot Fest co-founder who died in 2016.

Pezzati says the record sounds better than the band can play.

years.src: Psychedelic Baby
years.h: Pezzati reveals Kezdy and Spicer's card-game scam
years.p: Decades on, the band says the two had been cheating at Rummy 500 in the van with a foot-tapping system.
